rows.core: Saruman amasses Orcs when a noncreature spell is CAST with its mana value, even when alternate/reduced costs lower mana spent; repeated large-MV spells create Army damage.
rows.positive: Relic of Sauron is an artifact noncreature spell of mana value four, so casting it triggers Saruman and leaves repeatable UBR mana to pay future spells.
rows.cut_cost: Mana Geyser is mana value five, itself a substantial Amass increment while often producing much more mana from opponents' tapped lands on a decisive turn.
rules: Saruman triggers upon casting a noncreature spell; resolution or copying a spell is not a fresh cast.
The amass quantity uses mana value, not amount spent, so affinity, delve and alternate costs do not alter quantity by themselves.
Mana Geyser produces red mana equal to the number of tapped lands opponents control as it resolves.

Relic of Sauron costs four mana and has a tap ability adding {U}{B}{R}. As a noncreature artifact, it can normally tap immediately after resolving if it enters untapped and no other effect restricts it.
Saruman's Army may be a single Orc Army creature that grows with subsequent amass, not one separate new Army per spell.
rows.adverse: Relic can provide stable fixing, but trading a source-funded explosive mana spell and its higher amass for a generic four-mana rock may significantly lower lethal multi-spell turns.
rows.followup: Compare source-paid Saruman cast spell sequence with 4–12 opposing tapped lands, counting Army counters and real spells cast after resolving Geyser versus Relic.

rows.core: Parnesse turns copied instants and sorceries into political, optional opponent copies while taxing opposing spells/abilities targeting your permanents; own copy engines need mana for interaction.
rows.positive: Dimir Signet can supply both U and B using a generic payment, helping recast blue copy spells while holding black interaction.
rows.cut_cost: Talisman of Indulgence produces B or R without an activation mana input, sustaining red copy spells and interaction at lower upfront cost.
rules: Parnesse's opponent-copy ability rewards a player choosing to copy a spell you control; she does not mandate opponents to choose yes.
Dimir Signet requires spending {1}, then tapping, to produce {U}{B} and never directly generates red mana.
Talisman of Indulgence produces {B} or {R} for a life payment, or colorless without the life payment.
Swapping mana rocks does not increase Parnesse's spell-copy count unless it meaningfully changes available spell payments.
The first target-tax clause is triggered when opponents target you or your permanents and is not a mana ability of your rocks.
rows.adverse: The replacement can leave red copy and burn payoffs underfunded and demands another input source each tap; card swaps must be evaluated with the actual Grixis color curve.
rows.followup: Compute paid colored spell-copy turns at 2–5 mana with Signet versus Talisman under opponent responses and early red-pip requirements.

rows.core: Mishra's combat Warform copies noncreature artifacts as hasty 4/4 creatures, repeating artifact ETB/death/leaves triggers and enabling copy/sacrifice lines.
rows.positive: Thoughtcast can be one-blue mana with enough artifacts thanks to affinity, drawing two cards immediately during setup.
rows.cut_cost: Mystic Remora supplies early repeating cards from opponents casting noncreature spells, often replenishing the hand before a four-mana Mishra can be deployed.
rules: Mishra copies target noncreature artifact at beginning of combat, not sorceries like Thoughtcast.
Affinity for artifacts reduces generic mana cost of Thoughtcast based on artifacts controlled while casting; it cannot remove the blue pip.
The mana value of Thoughtcast remains five even when its payable cost is reduced.
Mystic Remora uses cumulative upkeep and triggers on opponent noncreature spells unless tax is paid; it may draw more than two over a turn cycle.
Mishra's copied Warform token is sacrificed at next end step, so its exits can feed artifact death/leave engines but do not directly cast Thoughtcast.
rows.adverse: One-shot two-card draw at potentially low cost can be reasonable in artifact-dense hands, yet cutting early recurring Remora sacrifices opponent-turn access to feed Mishra's artifact setup.
rows.followup: Count source artifact presence by turn and effective Thoughtcast payable mana, comparing Remora draws in pods with varying noncreature spell rates.

rows.core: Marchesa's dethrone/+1 counter package returns creatures that died with counters at beginning of next end step, enabling sacrifice loops and persist resets.
rows.positive: Village Rites is a one-black instant that sacrifices a countered creature and immediately draws two, an efficient way to trigger Marchesa recursion under stack pressure.
rows.cut_cost: Braids, Arisen Nightmare offers repeatable end-step sacrificing and multiplayer draw/punishment, which naturally exchanges expendable creatures for continuing recursion.
rules: Marchesa's return trigger requires the creature to have had a +1/+1 counter when it died while under your control, and the commander must control the relevant ability.
Village Rites sacrifices a creature as part of its additional casting cost and draws two on resolution.
Braids's end-step ability may sacrifice artifact, creature, enchantment, land or planeswalker, then pressures opponents to match the type or lose life and supply cards.
A creature returning at a later end step is not guaranteed to be present when a previous end-step sacrifice trigger is resolving.
Changing a repeating sacrifice engine to one-shot instant draw can reduce the available sacrifice events needed for persist/counter loops.
rows.adverse: Village Rites gives a flexible protection play, but Braids's sustained sacrifice cadence, opponent tax and refill are closely tied to Marchesa's sacrifice identity.
rows.followup: Trace countered creature death/return windows under free outlets plus Braids versus Rites and measure cards and reanimation steps in multiple turns.

rows.core: Equipped Tetsuo attacks to deal damage or cast an instant/sorcery with mana value no greater than the highest Equipment mana value attached; suspend/no-cast cost spells are premium choices.
rows.positive: Kiki-Jiki, Mirror Breaker can make a temporary hasty token copy of a creature with relevant ETB, if enough colored mana and untap opportunities exist.
rows.cut_cost: Sword of Fire and Ice is an Equipment that provides protection, combat damage to any target and card draw when equipped creature connects; its mana value also influences Tetsuo's free-cast ceiling.
rules: Tetsuo's trigger requires him to be equipped WHEN he attacks; unattached Kiki-Jiki offers no benefit to that trigger.
Kiki-Jiki's activation copies a nonlegendary creature you control, not Equipment or sorcery spells in hand.
The token copy Kiki-Jiki makes has haste but is sacrificed at the beginning of the next end step.
Sword of Fire and Ice has a mana value that can be used as Tetsuo's highest attached Equipment when it is equipped.
Tetsuo's combat free spell must be a legal instant or sorcery from hand within the mana value limit, not simply any copied creature.
rows.adverse: A generic triple-red creature copying engine loses equipped attack payoff, protection and free-spell threshold for an off-plan combo possibility.
rows.followup: Compare actual equipped Tetsuo attacks with Sword damage/draw and legal free-spell hits against source-paid Kiki-Jiki token lines.

rows.core: Missy turns dying nontoken nonartifact creatures into face-down Cybermen; controlled sac/turn-face-up loops exploit creature card characteristics carefully.
rows.positive: Darkwater Catacombs filters black and blue mana for early Missy casting and recursion outlets if current lands cannot produce both required colors.
rows.cut_cost: Otawara, Soaring City is an untapped blue source whose channel ability bounces an artifact, creature, enchantment or planeswalker without casting a spell; it can answer hate or preserve a combo creature.
rules: Missy triggers when a qualifying nonartifact creature dies and returns it face down as an artifact Cyberman; the death and return require proper zone ownership/control.
Turning a face-down Cyberman face up uses its actual applicable morph/disguise/turn-face-up costs and rules, not a general free flip.
Darkwater Catacombs requires another mana to activate and produces U/B; it cannot be counted as independent blue and black sources without the input.
Otawara's channel is an activated ability from hand and is not a spell; its blue mana land ability remains independently useful.
Replacing a channel answer with a filtering land can reduce ability to remove graveyard hate or reset a face-down loop under a timing window.
rows.adverse: The color filter competes with a low-opportunity-cost interactive channel land, a valuable safety valve while executing sacrifice/morph interactions.
rows.followup: Test a source-supported Missy face-up/death chain under graveyard hate and channel interaction, comparing mana-base source payments.
